To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the financial sector is a complex system, which can be studied with statistical data and models, but it requires a very high level of knowledge about the financial system, its institutions and their behavior, which is a very rare combination of skills and knowledge.
the macro-prudential policy requires a set of new, additional and/or more detailed data and models which can be used for analysis and policy making at macro level.
financial stability analysis and management requires data and models which are not yet available in most countries.

the following question: What are the main statistical data and models requirements in the macro prudential policy framework and how they are related to the traditional micro-level supervis

the following questions: what are the statistical data and models requirements for macro prudental analysis and policy making; what are the main challenges for national statistical systems; what are the possible solutions to overcome these challenges; what is the role of systemic risk models for macro prudetnal analysis; what are the expected problems with statistical data and models fulfillment and specification; what are the ways to overcome these problems.
the question how to improve the statistical data and models for the purpose of financial stability analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the macro prudential policy, in its essence, is a policy of the whole, and therefore, it requires the whole of data and models.

financial stability analysis is a very challenging and complex area of statistical and economic modeling, which is in constant development, with a lot of new data sources and models to be introduced in the near future.
the macro prudential policy requires a new approach to statistical data collection and modeling, which will bring a lot of new challenges to the statistical community and national authorities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

macro prudential policy and its statistical data requirements and models structure specifications are very important for the financial stability of any country, but they are not easy to implement and they bring some serious challenges to the statistical community.

macro prudential policies require a new approach to data and models, which should be based on the best available statistical data, which is a prerequisite for the development of a new generation of systemic risk models.

macro prudential policy and its analysis and management require a lot of data and models, which are not available at the present moment and which are not easy to be developed and implemented in the near future.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the financial sector is a special case of economic activity which requires a special approach to statistical data and modeling, and this is especially valid for financial stability analysis and policy making at macro level.
the financial stability analysis and policy making at the macro level requires new data and models which have to be built on top of the existing ones.
macro prudential policy and analysis is a new and challenging task for national and international statisticians and statistical data producers.
